narratives.Overview:
## Summary

v0.115.0 closed #4321 (Cursor dest-missing copy) and #4295 (dest-placing Cursor). A consumer still hits the same deny for write-capable `Task` from the **primary** checkout. The gate is correct. The deny text is not: it still names Task dest keys Cursor cannot send, and `CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY` still says continue-in-parent / explore / do-not-retry-plan. It does not name the two hatches #4295 shipped.

## Field instance

| | |
|---|---|
| **When** | 2026-09-10 / 2026-09-11 (after v0.115.0) |
| **Consumer** | [deftai/BestiMax](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax) |
| **Story** | [#321](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/321) — spellcheck for outgoing contractor messages |
| **Host** | Cursor, Multitask Mode, `Task` |
| **Parent workspace** | Primary checkout `/Users/baba/development/BestiMax` |
| **Intent** | Mutating roadmap ingest — proposed xBRIEF + `PROJECT-DEFINITION` |
| **Spawn** | `subagent_type: generalPurpose` (retry `best-of-n-runner`) |
| **Recorded on** | [#4321 comment 5627894787](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4321#issuecomment-5627894787) |

**Deny (class):**

```text
Directive denied implement-class spawn: no worktree destination on the spawn payload
(tool_input.isolation=worktree, worktree_path, cwd, …).
```

Subagents never started. Parent finished the ingest in linked worktree `.deft-scratch/worktrees/spellcheck-xbrief` via shell.

This is not a #4321 reopen. #4321 bound: no review-lane dest skip; write-capable Task stays on #4295. Doug's spawn was write work, so `explore` is the wrong class.

## Why the new release did not unblock this

- **#4321 in v0.115.0** only overlayed Cursor Task deny copy (`CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY`). It does not admit `generalPurpose` from primary.
- **#4295 in v0.115.0** admits one implement Task only when the **Composer window payload root is already a non-primary linked worktree** (nursery inherit), or via dest-rooted `@cursor/sdk` `Agent.create({ local: { cwd } })`. Consult returns null on the main worktree (`consultCursorNurseryInherit`: `isMainWorktreePath` → null → dest-missing).
- Doug's parent window was primary. Nursery inherit did not run. That is the designed fail-closed, not a deposit miss.

## Expected

Cursor Task dest-missing deny for implement-class must name **satisfiable** recoveries after #4295:

1. Continue in the parent (honest when the parent will do the writes).
2. Dest-place: open Composer on the reserved linked worktree, then at most one `Task` (nursery inherit).
3. Dest-rooted `@cursor/sdk` `Agent.create({ local: { cwd: <reserved-worktree> } })`.
4. `explore` only when the spawn is actually read-only.
5. Do not retry `plan` on Cursor Task.
6. Do not advertise `isolation` / `worktree_path` / `cwd` on Cursor Task as if the codec can send them.

Unmarked `generalPurpose` from primary stays dest-missing (#4066). Do not add a dest skip.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cursor Task dest-missing message names dest-placing (nursery window or SDK cwd), not Task dest keys as the recovery.
- [ ] `explore` remains qualified as read-only; `plan` is not advertised for Cursor Task.
- [ ] Tests: Cursor Task dest-missing fixture asserts dest-placing copy; implement Task from a linked payload root still nursery-allows.
- [ ] CHANGELOG + consumer note (BestiMax Multitask-from-primary).

Refs #4066 #4295 #4321 #4279

Disposition: retain the remedy, but describe opening Composer on the prepared non-primary linked worktree and allowing the existing launch flow to mint the unique reservation. The stronger alternative, a complete SDK setup workflow inside the deny message, would improve self-containment but duplicate the adapter and inflate this copy fix; a demonstrated inability to reach that adapter would change that tradeoff.

- `npx vitest run packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.test.ts packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts` at the pin SHA: **2 files, 77 tests, all pass.** Nothing in this issue is a currently-red test.

## Mechanism inventory (before proposing anything)

Everything this issue needs already exists. No new mechanism is warranted.

| Mechanism | Where | State |

## 1. blocks-the-design — the capability premise is recorded in-tree as deliberately unmeasured, and this issue re-asserts it as settled

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts:113-115` at the pin SHA:

```ts
const HOSTS_THAT_REROOT = new Set(["claude", "cursor", "codex"]);
// #4279: Cursor Task dest-key bind waits on a recorded PreToolUse payload.
// HOSTS_THAT_REROOT for Task stays unbound until that measurement.
```

`CHANGELOG.md`, `## [0.115.0] - 2026-09-10`, the #4279 entry: *"Cursor Task isolation-key bind stays unbound until a PreToolUse measurement."* That is the shipped position of the very release this issue is filed against.

The predicate is not neutral on this. `cursor` is in `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT`, so `hostCanReroot` is true (`spawn-occupancy.ts:434`), so a pathless `isolation: "worktree"` on Cursor **allows** and the hook supplies the path — the `destPath === null && !hostCanReroot` deny just below it never fires for Cursor. `isolation=worktree` is precisely the token that flips this deny to allow, *if* the codec forwards it.

The field record does not measure it. [#4321 comment 5627894787](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4321#issuecomment-5627894787) records `Task` with `subagent_type: generalPurpose` and a prompt. No dest key was attempted. A deny on a payload that carried no dest key is silent on whether a payload carrying one would arrive with it.

**Failure mode.** Acceptance 1 and Expected 6 are stated on the codec-capability claim ("Task dest keys Cursor cannot send" / "as if the codec can send them"). Bind them and the tree contradicts itself in three places at once: the deny says the keys are unsendable, `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT` says Cursor reroots, and the CHANGELOG says the question is open. If the measurement later lands the other way, the copy is newly dishonest and #4362 has to be reverted rather than extended.

**Disposition consequence.** As written the lean cannot bind. It does not need the measurement in order to bind — see the steelman below — but it does need to stop resting on it.

## 2. blocks-the-design — advertising nursery inherit as *the* recovery fences the parent out of the tree it is already using

**Evidence.** `applyCursorNurseryOccupancy` is verified to deny the parent's own product writes once the child grant is live: `spawn-occupancy.test.ts:1340-1381`, ending `expect(fenced.allow).toBe(false); expect(fenced.message).toMatch(/nursery occupancy grant is live/)`. `host-cursor.md:22` states the same in prose: *"While that grant is live, parent product writes in that tree are denied."*

Read the field instance against that. The parent was in primary, and it finished the ingest **itself, by shell, in `.deft-scratch/worktrees/spellcheck-xbrief`** — the reserved linked worktree. Acceptance 1 mandates that the deny name dest-placing as the recovery: open Composer on that reserved worktree, then one `Task`. A parent that follows that instruction converts its own working tree into a fenced nursery and loses the exact path that actually succeeded.

Second half of the same problem: opening a Composer window on a different folder is an **operator** action. The deny is consumed by the model. A model-facing deny whose headline recovery the model cannot itself perform yields a stall or a hallucinated "I opened the window", not a recovery.

**Failure mode.** Parent reads the new copy, relocates into the nursery, spawns the one admitted Task; child holds the grant; the parent's follow-up writes in that tree now deny with `nursery occupancy grant is live`. Two denies where there was one, and the working fallback talked out of.

**Disposition consequence.** Acceptance 1 cannot bind as a flat "name dest-placing, not dest keys". The copy has to separate agent-executable recoveries (continue in the parent; assist/ephemeral; `explore` when genuinely read-only) from operator-required dest-placing, and it has to state the fence — that dest-placing hands that tree to the child. This is not "a reviewer would catch it": the fence predicate already exists and is already tested, and the deterministic control is that the copy must quote its consequence.

## 3. sharpens-framing — the defect is not in `CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY`, and the acceptance tests as written cannot detect the fix

**Evidence.** The dest-key list appears **twice** in the emitted message (probe above): once as diagnosis, once as the imperative *"Pass a destination field inspectSpawnDestination reads (...) before the spawn primitive."* That imperative is the unsatisfiable instruction, and it lives in `rerootMissingDestMessage()` (`spawn-occupancy.ts:272`), not in the recovery constant. `overlayCursorTaskSpawnRecovery` only `String.replace`s `SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY` / `SPAWN_READ_ONLY_RECOVERY` (`dispatcher.ts:294-299`), so it cannot reach it.

`rerootMissingDestMessage()` is host-blind and serves `claude` and `codex` too; `spawn-occupancy.test.ts:103` (*"allows Claude isolation=worktree without a concrete path"*) shows the copy is honest for at least one of them.

And the #4279 honesty lock does **not** block the fix, contrary to how the write-back frames it. `dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts:645-660` and `spawn-occupancy.test.ts:1222-1229` assert `toContain(key)`. Because the keys appear twice, deleting the imperative occurrence leaves every one of those assertions green.

**Failure mode.** Two ways to get this wrong from the acceptance text as written. Edit only `CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY` and the false imperative survives verbatim — the shipped fix does not fix the reported defect. Or edit `rerootMissingDestMessage()` globally and regress Claude/Codex copy. Either way the acceptance test criterion ("fixture asserts dest-placing copy") passes, because containment assertions cannot see a removal.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean binds, but the build note must name the seam and the tests must be stated as exclusions, not inclusions: export the imperative sentence as a named constant so the overlay has an anchor, keep host+tool scoping in the overlay (see road-not-taken), and add `expect(message).not.toContain("before the spawn primitive")` next to the positive dest-placing assertion, plus a Claude/Codex fixture asserting the imperative *survives* there.

## 4. sharpens-framing — the SDK hatch chains a second fail-closed

**Evidence.** `host-cursor.md:23` conditions the headless path on doctor check `cursor-sdk-auth` and a separate `CURSOR_API_KEY` login; the check is real (`packages/core/src/doctor/checks.ts:1451`). Expected item 3 advertises `Agent.create({ local: { cwd } })` unconditionally.

**Failure mode.** A consumer with no `CURSOR_API_KEY` follows recovery 3 out of a dest deny and lands in an auth failure with no pointer back. The deny will have spent its one shot at directing the agent.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean binds; recovery 3 must carry its precondition inline (`deft doctor` → `cursor-sdk-auth`, separate SDK login) rather than sitting flat beside continue-in-parent.

## 5. sharpens-framing — "after v0.115.0" is inference, not record

**Evidence.** The deny quoted in the body and in [comment 5627894787](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4321#issuecomment-5627894787) is labelled **"Deny (class)"** and reads `(tool_input.isolation=worktree, worktree_path, cwd, ...)` — three keys and an ellipsis. v0.115.0's #4279 change emits **nine** keys (probe above). The cited comment dates the instance 2026-09-10; v0.115.0 is dated 2026-09-10.

**Failure mode.** "Why the new release did not unblock this" is the load-bearing section, and its only evidence is a paraphrase fully compatible with a pre-#4279 build. If the consumer was on 0.114.x, the correct disposition is a version-confirmation ask, not a recut.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean binds either way — the copy gap at the pin SHA is real and I confirmed it by execution, not by the field report. But the framing should either drop the release-regression claim or the write-back should record the consumer's installed version.

## 6. sharpens-framing (protocol) — Stop 3's ⊗ on parent hypotheses is defeated by the round-1 ceiling

**Evidence.** `content/contracts/design-critique.md` Stop 3: *"⊗ Load parent hypotheses into the envelope"* and *"⊗ Name a refutation target unless the recorded variant is refutation."* My envelope complies — charter `open critique`, no refutation target. But Stop 1 MUSTs `refutation-target:` on the write-back unconditionally, and *"Round-1 ceiling is the triage write-back when one exists."* The write-back at 5628477283 records `charter: open critique` **and** a full-sentence `refutation-target:`. Honoring the ceiling therefore means reading the parent hypothesis the envelope rule exists to withhold. The arc section even states *"Open critique names no refutation target"*, which the Stop 1 MUST contradicts.

**Failure mode.** Every open-critique round-1 critic is anchored on the parent's asserted premise while the contract records that it is not. No gate observes this, so the drift is silent.

**Disposition consequence.** Not #4362's build. Either scope the Stop 1 MUST to the refutation charter, or state in Stop 3 that the ⊗ is envelope-only and the write-back is in-envelope by ceiling. Worth its own issue, not a rider here.

## Injection / swarm lens

Fires: this target changes model-facing envelope text on a spawn authority boundary.

- **No untrusted-input path today, and the fix must not open one.** `rerootMissingDestMessage()` interpolates only compile-time key lists. Dest-placing copy is tempting to write as "open Composer on `<reserved worktree>`" with a payload-derived path. Do not. `payloadRoot` is host-supplied; echoing it into instruction text puts caller-influenced bytes inside a directive the model is told to follow. Keep the new copy static, as `grokMissingDestMessage()` and both existing recovery constants already are.
- **Occupancy / identity.** Covered in finding 2. The grant is keyed on `canonicalHostSessionId` and is same-host only — `applyCursorNurseryOccupancy` refuses a `grok` child and a foreign session (`spawn-occupancy.test.ts:1359-1370`). That fence is correct; the defect is that the copy would advertise entry into it without stating the cost.
- **Worktrees.** Unmarked `generalPurpose` from primary staying dest-missing is right and nothing here touches it. This critique proposes no dest skip.
- **Concurrency.** A second `Task` in the same nursery window is `reservation-conflict` (`spawn-occupancy.ts:392-402`, tested at `spawn-occupancy.test.ts:1308`). If the copy says "then at most one `Task`", it should say why, or a parent that fans out will read the conflict deny as a bug.

## Road not taken

I considered emitting Cursor-specific copy from `consultImplementSpawnOccupancy` directly — the `grokMissingDestMessage()` pattern, cleaner than a post-hoc `String.replace` that silently no-ops if the source sentence is ever reworded. Rejected: consult receives `host` but not `toolName`, and `SPAWN_TOOL_NAMES` (`hooks/tools.ts:22`) carries five spellings (`Task`, `SubagentStart`, `spawn_subagent`, `start_agent`, `CreateAgent`). Host-only scoping would apply Cursor-Task copy to any other spawn spelling arriving under `host: "cursor"`. The overlay is the only seam with both host and tool. Keep it; give it an exported anchor for the imperative sentence.

## Steelman of the position I am blocking, and what flips finding 1

The strongest case against finding 1: the measurement is irrelevant, because `host-cursor.md:15` already reads *"⊗ Dispatch local implement via Cursor `Task` dest keys, a worktree map in the prompt, or inherited primary cwd."* That is doctrine, not capability. Even if Cursor forwards `isolation` perfectly, Directive has already forbidden that route — so a deny instructing the agent to take it is wrong regardless of what the codec does, and the copy fix is warranted today.

I find that persuasive. **It flips finding 1 to non-blocking the moment the lean is restated on the ⊗ instead of on the codec.** The two framings produce the same string and different futures: the doctrine framing survives the measurement landing either way and needs no revert; the capability framing collides with `spawn-occupancy.ts:113-115` and the v0.115.0 CHANGELOG line right now, and inverts outright if the measurement comes back positive. Change Acceptance 1 and Expected 6 from *"keys Cursor cannot send"* to *"a route #4295 doctrine forbids"*, leave `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT` and the #4279 measurement debt untouched and explicitly out of scope, and finding 1 is discharged without waiting on anything.

## Footnotes

- `footnote` — The write-back attributes the primary-checkout null to `consultCursorNurseryInherit`'s `isMainWorktreePath` guard. The guard that actually fires first is `isLinkedWorktreePath(payloadRoot)` (`spawn-occupancy.ts:373`), false for a primary checkout because `.git` is a directory there (`session/main-worktree.ts:32`). `isMainWorktreePath` is the second-line defense for a linked-looking path. Same outcome, different line; matters only if someone builds a test from the cited guard.
- `footnote` — Nothing binds the deny copy to `host-cursor.md` Step 2e. After this fix the two can drift with no gate. Not worth a mechanism; worth a cross-reference comment at the constant.
- `footnote` — The message is already ~900 characters before adding three hatches and an SDK signature. Expected lists six items, two of them prohibitions. If all six land verbatim the deny roughly doubles. Consider whether prohibitions 5 and 6 need to be in the wire text at all, given `CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY` already carries the `plan` prohibition.
- `footnote` — Spend is N>=3 with families grok, claude, codex. The panel-deposit MUST is a GitHub comment, which necessarily sits above ceiling 5628477283, so I cannot confirm it exists. Recorded as a limit of the envelope, not as a finding.
